samples.xml_description:
<module id="multi_8bit">
    <description>Implement an 8-bit multiplier based on shifting and adding operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[7:0]">First 8-bit input operand (multiplicand).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[7:0]">Second 8-bit input operand (multiplier).</input>
        <output id="product" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit output representing the product of A and B.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="N" value="8">Parameter N represents the number of bits for inputs A and B.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <variable id="i" type="integer">Loop index for iterating through the bits of input B.</variable>
        <variable id="shifted_A" width_description="[15:0]">Temporary variable to store the shifted multiplicand A.</variable>
        <variable id="product_temp" width_description="[15:0]">Temporary variable to store the intermediate product.</variable>
        <statement>
            Initialize i to 0 and product_temp to 0.
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                if (B[i] == 1) begin
                    product_temp = product_temp + (A << i);
                end
            end
            shifted_A = A << 1;
            for (i = 1; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                if (B[i] == 1) begin
                    product_temp = product_temp + shifted_A;
                end
                shifted_A = shifted_A << 1;
            end
            product = product_temp;
        </statement>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        The module performs multiplication of A and B using the shift-and-add method.
        - The algorithm iterates through each bit of the multiplier (B).
        - For each bit that is set (1), the multiplicand (A) is added to the product at the corresponding shifted position.
        - The process continues until all bits of the multiplier have been processed.
        - Shifting: After each addition, the multiplicand is logically shifted left by one bit to prepare for the next addition.
        - The final product is stored in the output port, which is 16 bits wide to accommodate the maximum possible product of two 8-bit numbers.
    </implementation>
</module>
